 Agglomerative is an unsupervised clustering based algorithm. It starts with each individual items in its own cluster and iteratively merge until all the only one cluster remains.

It assumes that the set of elements and the distance between them is given as input. We use n x n vertex adjacency matrix, A, as input. it contains distance value rather than the simple boolean value. The simple boolean value just indicates whether the nodes are connected with each other or not, instead of using this, we replace boolean '1' with the actual distance between each nodes.

The output of the agglomerative clustering algorithm is a dendrogram, a set of triple <d,k,K> where d is a threshold distance, k is the number of clusters, and K is the set of Clusters.

dendrogram:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Linkages method determine, how the distance between clusters is calculated during the merging process.

  Linkage: Distance between two clusters is defined as the shortest distance between two points in a cluster. This forms chain like structure. If cluster A has two points {A1,A2} and cluster B has {B1,B2} then the distance between the cluster A, B will the

minimum(distance(A1, B1), distance(A1, B2), distance(A2, B1), distance(A2, B2)).

Complete Linkage: Distance between two clusters will be defined as the longest distance between points in both the clusters. This forms a compact spherical cluster. If cluster A has two points {A1,A2} and cluster B has {B1,B2} then the distance between the cluster A, B will the

maximum(distance(A1, B1), distance(A1, B2), distance(A2, B1), distance(A2, B2)).

Average Linkage: Distance between two clusters is defined as the average of all the pairwise distances between each points. Balances between Single and Complete Linkage. If cluster A has two points {A1,A2} and cluster B has {B1,B2} then the distance between the cluster A, B will the

average(distance(A1, B1), distance(A1, B2), distance(A2, B1), distance(A2, B2)).
